summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for a severe flare of right sacroiliac joint pain following a recent upper respiratory infection and initiation of Simponi therapy. He reported worsening pain after starting Simponi, along with fungal intertrigo in the right inguinal fold. He was treated with a three-day course of high-dose IV steroids, which significantly improved his pain without requiring an oral steroid taper. The intertrigo was managed with miconazole powder, and his home medications for hypertension, asthma, anxiety, and pain were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with rheumatology and infectious disease, continue Simponi, and monitor for recurrent symptoms.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
